This indicates that Ethosuximide may indirectly affect Cyp3a7-cyp3a51p through the activation of Cyp3a43 or via the binding of Lercanidipine, which itself is bound to Cyp3a7-cyp3a51p. The shared involvement of Cyp3a7-cyp3a51p in both pathways highlights a potential role in drug metabolism, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The integration of these pathways underscores the complex interplay between Ethosuximide and Cyp3a7-cyp3a51p, emphasizing the importance of considering both direct and indirect interactions in understanding drug-target relationships.
